text: Lynn Conway was born in Mount Vernon, New York, in 1938. She grew up in Hartsdale and White Plains, New York, and experienced gender dysphoria as a child. After leaving MIT in 1959, she pursued a career in engineering and technology. In 1964, she joined IBM Research, where she worked on advanced supercomputer architecture and developed dynamic instruction scheduling. In 1968, she was fired after revealing her intention to transition. After detransitioning, she worked as a contract programmer and later joined Xerox PARC, where she co-authored *Introduction to VLSI Systems* with Carver Mead. She founded the multiproject wafers (MPW) technology and developed the MOSIS system, which revolutionized VLSI design and enabled access to state-of-the-art digital technology for universities and small companies. Conway retired from active research in 1998 at the University of Michigan. She was a pioneer in VLSI design and received numerous awards, including the IEEE EAB Major Educational Innovation Award, Fellow of the IEEE, and the IEEE/RSE James Clerk Maxwell Medal. In 2023, she was inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame. Conway also became a prominent transgender rights activist, advocating for equal opportunities and employment protections for transgender people in the tech industry. She co-founded the "Transsexual Women's Successes" website and was named one of the "Stonewall 40 trans heroes" in 2009. She passed away in June 2024 at the age of 86.
